title.narrative: Pathway 3: Policy advocacy (linked to MFA standard indicator SCS 4)

description.narrative: Governments adopt, implement and account for human rights-based policies and laws that enable young people’s SRHR and gender justice

title.narrative: 3.2.1 Number of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at sub-national level

description.narrative: # of advocacy initiatives carried by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at sub-national level

comment.narrative: The baseline value is set to 0 as this indicator measures changes implemented by the programme during its lifetime.

2021: This includes various orientation meeting. One advocacy initative includes meetings with decision-makers in the provinces and districts about the RHRN agenda and the possibility of school intervention in 3 districts of 3 provinces (Langkat, Indramayu, Jombang). Another advocacy initiative includes a series of discussions on the urgency of local regulation draft (Raperda) of the Prevention and Overcoming of Sexual Deviant Behavior in Bogor City.2022: This included various meetings with local government, stakeholder meetings at local level, programme launches in specific areas. 2023 (first half): This included various meetings with local government stakeholders including Ministry of Religious Affairs in Jombang, District Education and Culture Office in Jombang, etc.

2023 (second half): Total 10. This includes dissemination of DIM Perda P4S Bogor City, Coordination meeting with stakeholders in Langkat, Indramayu, Jombang, etc.2024: Total 30. This includes multi-sector stakeholder meetings in Indramayu district and Jombang district regarding local policies regarding young people's SRHR and CSE.
This target was adjusted based on MTR process

description.narrative: # of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their constituencies at all other levels

2021: Advocacy initiatives ranged from orientation meetings with state actors, dissemination of research findings on LTO1, and developing CSE for out of school youth.2022: This included the UPR webinar.2023 (first half): This included the focus group discussion on challenges in implementing the TPKS Law

2023 (second half): Total 5. This includes lobbying for derivative regulations from the TPKS law, and national advocacy for the two Ministries regulations2024. Total 9. This includes coordination with the Ministry of Education on Violence Prevention and Handling Program in the Education Unit Environment (PPKSP Program) for the implementation of Permendikbud No. 46 of 2023 as well as coordination with the Ministry of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection to support the establishment of UPTD PPA in Indramayu Regency.

title.narrative: 3.1.1 Changes in (decision making towards) policies (adoption, adaptation, maintaining, blocking), in line with the RHRN2 agenda

description.narrative: # of governmental policies blocked, adopted, improved or maintained, in line with the RHRN2 agenda

comment.narrative: The baseline value is set to 0 as this indicator measures changes implemented by the programme during its lifetime.

2023 (first half): (1) Head of the Jombang District Education Office, East Java) issued a Circular Letter on Handling Bullying and sexual harassment in Schools; (2) MoU between Jombang District Government and Rutgers Indonesia

2023 (second half): (1) Formation of the PPK Team in Jombang Regency and overseeing the preparation of the Regent's Decree for the PPK Team; (2) On August 14, 2023, Mr. Alpin (Head of Pantai Gemi Village), Mr. Sugiono (Head of Sidomulyo Urban Village), and Mrs. Kartini Br Sembiring, S.H (Head of Kwala Bingai Urban Village) signed a decree regarding the establishment of a youth integrated service post (posyandu).2024: (1) On August 30, 2024, Mr. Muhajir (Head of the Jombang Regency Ministry of Religious Affairs Office (MoRA) issued a Circular to form a sexual violence handling unit at the Education Unit under the Ministry of Religious Affairs. (2) On October 9, 2024, Mr. DR. H. Caridin, M.Si (Head of the Indramayu District Education Office) signed a Circular Letter regarding the Implementation of Reproductive Health and Sexuality Education (PKRS) addressed to 216 Junior High Schools (SMP) throughout Indramayu District.

2024: (1) On May 27, 2024, Mrs. Asmaliah (Vice Chairman of Commission C of the Regional House of Representatives (DPRD) of Langkat Regency) invited ASB and CIKAL youth to participate in a public consultation on the Draft Regional Regulation (Ranperda). This is the first time that the Legislative of Langkat Regency invited young people to participate in the decision-making process. (2) On 3 December 2024, WCC Jombang and Inclusion Alliance (In Indonesian: Aliansi Inklusi) invited by Imam Kurniawan, expert staff for drafting laws and the legal team of the Jombang Regional Government to discuss in the preparation of the draft regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children in Jombang. (3) On 19 July 2024, the Pantai Gemi Village Government of Langkat Regency invited Agung Prasetyo and Naisa Bila, one of the young people of CIKAL, to the Development Planning Deliberation (Musrenbang) activity. This is the first time the Pantai Gemi Village Government of Langkat Regency has invited young people to participate in the decision-making process.
